audit.source_of_truth: CSV for values and structure; Guidebook for definitions and collection/processing description

group_split_suitability.reason: SerialNo grouping prevents the same product number from crossing train/test, but every repeated SerialNo has conflicting labels; the product-level label contract must be clarified before a defensible supervised evaluation.

near_zero_variance.criterion: non-constant; unique percentage <= 10% and most-common/second-most-common frequency ratio > 19

matched: SerialNo is object and defined as product number
ReceivedDateTime is object in the raw CSV and all values parse as datetime
max / mean / min / std feature families
13 constant numeric columns; after dropping constants and two object columns, 28 columns remain
All observed timestamps fall within the stated 2022-08-23 through 2022-08-27 validity interval
inconsistencies: upper_mold_temp1 is listed among the final 9 variables but is absent from the 43-column CSV; no substitute was inferred.
The guidebook states a collection period through 2022-08-27, while the latest timestamp actually present is 2022-08-25 10:14:44.102 (the values are within, but do not cover, the full stated period).

The guidebook states one row represents one product and SerialNo is the product number, but 99 SerialNo values each occur twice at the same timestamp with conflicting 0/1 labels and different feature vectors.
The guidebook reports SerialNo uniqueness as 90.9%, which matches 986/1,085, but does not explain the conflicting labels for repeated SerialNo values.

leakage_risks.finding: 99 product identifiers repeat; a row split can place the same SerialNo and timestamp in both train and test.
All 99 repeated SerialNo groups contain both PASS and FAIL; label resolution cannot be inferred safely.
Only three observed dates are present; random mixing can hide day/batch drift.
Selecting variables by T-test on all rows before splitting uses evaluation labels.
Synthetic samples created before split would leak training information into evaluation.
Imputation, scaling/normalization, outlier thresholds, constant filtering, and selection must be fit on training data only.

safe_ml_evaluation_design: First obtain an authoritative rule for the 99 conflicting SerialNo labels; do not silently deduplicate or relabel.
Keep all rows sharing a SerialNo in one fold using a group-aware split; validate that no SerialNo overlaps folds.
Add a forward temporal holdout by ReceivedDateTime where sample size permits; report the narrow three-day coverage.
Fit feature selection, outlier rules, imputation, scaling/normalization, and SMOTE only inside each training fold.
Apply SMOTE only to training partitions after the split; never to validation/test data.
Report class-aware metrics and confidence intervals, not accuracy alone.

CNC_Adapter_PoC.reason: The raw schema, types, feature families, timestamp parsing, and row-level records are usable for an isolated adapter, provided the adapter preserves rows and exposes label conflicts without resolving them.

Ground_Truth_Context_PoC.reason: The official 0/1 meaning is clear, but 99 product identifiers have conflicting labels.

CNC_RAG_PoC.reason: The Guidebook is a useful official reference, but retrieval answers must surface the upper_mold_temp1 and SerialNo/label inconsistencies.

simple_ML_Baseline_PoC.reason: A guarded experiment is possible only after label handling is explicitly decided and group/temporal leakage controls are applied.

DNN_performance_evaluation.reason: 1,085 rows, only 99 FAIL rows, a three-day observed period, and unresolved product-level label conflicts do not support a reliable DNN performance claim.

Production_generalization_claim.reason: No independent site/machine/time-period holdout exists, and product-level ground truth is unresolved.

verdict.meaning: The read-only audit completed and the inconsistencies are explicitly captured; PASS is not a claim that the dataset is production-ready.
guardrails: Do not collapse SerialNo to one row or infer a replacement label.
Expose conflicting-label status in the adapter contract.
Do not start ML evaluation until the ground-truth conflict has an authoritative resolution.
